Remediation Playbook Templates

Content Version: 26.2.0

Overview This playbook provides a foundational suite of non-functional template flows designed to accelerate incident response and remediation processes. Rather than dictating specific tools, these templates serve as a customizable, vendor-agnostic baseline. Security teams can use these structural frameworks as a starting point to easily configure, map, and deploy automated actions using their integrations of choice and specific operational requirements.

Included Template Flows

  • Observable Remediation - Block: A framework for blocking malicious observables (e.g., IPs, domains, URLs, file hashes) across your designated network, web gateway, or endpoint security controls.

  • Observable Remediation - Unblock: A template to reverse the blocking of observables, allowing teams to quickly mitigate false positives or restore normal operations once a threat is neutralized.

  • User Account - Block: A workflow structure designed to disable, suspend, or lock compromised user accounts within your Identity and Access Management (IAM) or Active Directory environments.

  • User Account - Unblock: A template for restoring standard user account access following successful remediation, password resets, or identity verification.

  • Revoke Access Tokens: A baseline flow intended to force session termination and revoke active authentication tokens (e.g., OAuth, SSO sessions) to immediately halt unauthorized access.

  • Isolate Host: A framework for containing a potentially compromised endpoint. Once configured with your EDR/XDR tool, this flow cuts off external network connectivity while preserving secure access for forensic investigation.

  • Release Host: A template to lift isolation protocols and restore standard network connectivity to an endpoint once it has been sanitized, patched, and cleared by the security team.

Configuration Guidelines

Important Note: These flows are provided as functionally inactive templates.

To utilize these flows in a production environment, clients must:

  1. Select Integrations: Add/Swap out actions with your specific security integrations (e.g., CrowdStrike, Palo Alto Networks, Okta, Microsoft Entra ID).

  2. Map Variables: Configure the necessary inputs, outputs, and authentication credentials for your environment.

  3. Test: Run the modified flows in a staging or testing environment to ensure they align with internal security policies and do not disrupt critical business operations.
